That sticky stop is costing you in North Texas jackpots and it's not because he forgot how to rate.

When the hindquarters can't load and fire the way they're built to, the stop gets flat. The power leaks. You feel it — that half-second of nothing when you ask.

Dr. Leo sees this every week on DFW ranch horses and barrel horses that have been hauling hard since spring. A locked sacrum or tight lumbar doesn't just look like stiffness at the walk. It shows up at the moment your run depends on it most.

If your horse used to stop like a freight train and now he's just coasting in, get him checked before you chalk it up to attitude or arena footing.
